analysis: Both changed files are test or comment-only. In LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (head lines 181-203), a new test checks that DeadlineAdmissionFixes.environmentKey is in LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys, is not in WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys, and that the plist forwards only that key. It also checks that the "UNRELATED_SECRET" entry is excluded, that the default resolves to enabled, and that "0" and "off" disable it. The test reinforces the existing allowlist-based environment passthrough and does not widen it. Production code was not supplied, so the test's claim that the key is in the allowlist cannot be verified here. That key is a performance/availability knob for deadline admission estimator corrections. It does not touch attestation, encryption, authorization, or A-001 data handling. ServingQualificationDeadlineEvidence.swift (head lines 5-10) only gains a doc-comment clarification that calibrated requests get no per-batch decode shape, and it changes no logic. No new attack surface, no threat-model assumption invalidated, and no regression identified. Open question for integration: the production-side implementation of DeadlineAdmissionFixes (resolve semantics, handling of the raw value "off\n", and the decodeRateShape change) is not in this batch. Whether a provider operator disabling the correction through the environment could affect T-007 or T-010 availability-style behavior is outside the supplied evidence. Since the operator already controls the provider, this is not a boundary change.
